principles.statement: Taking a lock guard in the same expression that awaits a function which loops until stopped means the guard is held for the life of the task.
principles.rationale: Live 2026-09-20: `integrity.write().await.start_monitoring()` held the write guard across the monitoring loop forever; the first other-path `read()` blocked permanently, hanging every container update and, through a downstream fan-out, every pipeline execution behind the executor lock.

principles.statement: Prefer interior mutability for long-lived services: a monitor whose state is Arc/RwLock inside only ever needs the outer guard for the duration of a method call, not the duration of its life.
principles.rationale: start_monitoring(&self) only needed &self — the outer write guard was never required at all; a read guard held forever is safe because nothing else writes the outer lock.

principles.statement: A hang is not load. Suites green while production deadlocks means the test built its own fixture and never exercised the shared lock in loop conditions.
principles.rationale: The deadlock shipped with a fully green suite: every test constructed its own monitor and none ran the monitor loop concurrently with a snapshot caller.

heuristics.name: Spawning a task that runs a service loop.
heuristics.description: Audit every guard acquired in the spawn expression: if the awaited call loops indefinitely, the guard must be unnecessary for the call (interior mutability) or the loop must not hold it.

heuristics.name: Diagnosing a system-wide hang with green tests.
heuristics.description: Trace lock acquisition order across the hang path; check specifically for guards whose scope spans an unbounded await.

decision_rules.condition: A method that runs an unbounded loop needs a lock to start.
decision_rules.action: Verify the loop only needs &self with interior state locks, and take the weakest guard (read) for the shortest scope the borrow checker allows.
